subject: Temporary BYOK retention carveout — triage & product asks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Novak <claire@medalign.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary BYOK retention carveout — triage & product asks

Hi team,

Following up from the MedAlign intake (cc'd) — they need a short-term BYOK retention carveout for a pilot. Key asks from the customer: 1) a temporary retention window of 30 days for decrypted request logs while they complete an internal audit, 2) a KMS rotation window during which keys can be rotated without breaking sessions, and 3) assurance that audit logs include per-request key-id and rotation events.

Questions for triage:
- Feasibility: can we support a 30-day temporary retention of decrypted request metadata for a specific tenant (MedAlign) without a full product rollout?
- Risk: what are the smallest scoped code/config changes to enable this as an exception (ideally a config flag per account + audit gating)?
- Monitoring: what additional audit log fields do we need to emit (key-id, rotation-timestamp, action:encrypt/decrypt/rotate, actor)?
- Timeline: what is the earliest we can propose to MedAlign for a pilot?

I've attached the completed intake form (byok-carveout-form.pdf) and a short internal note listing the customer constraints (link below). I'd like to make a go/no-go decision by Thursday EOD so Claire can get procurement moving.

Can Ben and Marissa take the lead on feasibility + risk assessment? Grace, can you confirm observable/audit requirements and a suggested retention policy enforcement plan? Jonas — please confirm whether an ops playbook for ephemeral escrow is already available or needs drafting.

Claire — thanks for starting the intake. If anything critical is missing in the form, flag it here.

Next step: if people can, let's do a 30-minute triage call tomorrow (Wed 11/11) — I put a placeholder in the doc.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Novak <claire@medalign.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary BYOK retention carveout — triage & product asks

Thanks Priya — good summary. Quick thoughts from product/compliance perspective:

- Short-term approach: I think we can support a limited carveout as an account-scoped feature flag backed by an exception registry. Implementation would be two parts: (1) allow an account-level retention override in the retention service, and (2) gate the override behind an approvals step (manual + audit trail).
- Scope/lifetime: we should require a defined expiration on the override (30 days in this case) and an automatic rollback when it expires.
- UI/workflow: we can surface the exception in Console > Security > Exceptions so CS/procurement can confirm.

Risks / blockers:
- We need engineering time for a safer rollout — the main blocker is ensuring that the override cannot be applied broadly by mistake (need RBAC + approval flow).
- We should not change default behavior for the hosted runtime; this must be an explicit per-account opt-in with documented controls.

I've attached a short draft (kb-byok-workaround.md) describing a temporary escrow flow that would avoid long-term code changes: ephemeral escrow + explicit audit events. Ben — can you validate the escape hatch from an ops perspective (is it viable for customer sessions today)?

If we get a green light, product can scope a minimal UI and an end-to-end acceptance test for the pilot.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Compliance

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Claire Novak <claire@medalign.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary BYOK retention carveout — triage & product asks

Heads-up on ops feasibility after a quick sweep with the infra team:

- KMS rotation window: we can support a configurable rotation window per account (e.g., tolerate key rotation within a 24h drift for active sessions) by tracking key-id in the session metadata and allowing a short grace period where both old and new keys are accepted for decryption. This requires small changes to session key resolution logic and the key service (estimate: 3-5 dev days + 2 days staging validation).

- Audit logs: we can emit the following minimal fields for the pilot: request_id, account_id, timestamp, key_id, key_rotation_event (old_key->new_key with timestamp), action_type (encrypt/decrypt), request_path. We should also redact PII in logs as usual.

- Temporary retention: retaining decrypted request metadata for 30 days for a single account is feasible if we store only metadata (no request payloads) and enforce the expiration automatically. Ops needs a DB-backed flag to drive the behavior; can be backward-compatible with current retention jobs.

Blockers/Concerns:
- Escrow pattern: ephemeral escrow (customer supplies temp key and we hold it in an HSM-backed escrow during the window) is conceptually fine but increases attack surface — we should require an SOC review if we go that route beyond pilot.
- SLA/rollback: need a rollback plan if the override is misapplied. Suggest logging all approval actions in an immutable audit index.

I'll open SUP-4821 to track the infra changes and include a brief implementation plan. Tentative ETA for a pilot branch + staging test: 3 weeks from approval (assuming we prioritize).

Ben Carter
Security & Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Claire Novak <claire@medalign.com>, procurement@medalign.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary BYOK retention carveout — triage & product asks

Thanks all — this is helpful. Short summary and decisions:

- Scope: we will approve a 30-day account-scoped retention override for MedAlign as a pilot. The override will be explicit, expire automatically after 30 days, and require two approvers from Product/Compliance + Security.
- Implementation owners: Ben (infrastructure) will own SUP-4821 for the KMS/session changes and audit events. Marissa will own the exception workflow + Console surface. Grace will own the observable schema and verification tests. I will coordinate the acceptance criteria and customer comms.
- Customer-facing ETA: propose pilot kickoff week of 2026-12-06, dependent on SUP-4821 PR & staging tests.
- Risk controls: require manual approval steps recorded in the immutable audit index; do not enable as default. Require SOC review if the escrow pattern is used beyond the pilot.

Claire/procurement — please confirm that the pilot timeline is acceptable so we can proceed to internal approvals.

Next actions:
- Ben: open and assign SUP-4821 with the infra estimate (you mentioned 3-5 dev days + validation).
- Marissa: draft the Console exception UI spec and the approval flow doc.
- Grace: publish the audit schema and an acceptance test checklist.
- Priya: book a 30-min kickoff the first week of Dec — calendar link: https://redwood.calendar/meet/triage-call-20261111.

Attaching the intake form again for records: byok-carveout-form.pdf

Thanks — will follow up once SUP-4821 is live.

Priya Natarajan
Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
